Introduction

This document describes the system register specifications of PS3111.

Overview

System Block Diagram

The block diagram of System (PD0, PD1) is shown as figure 1.

Figure 1: The system block diagram of System (PD0, PD1)

Base Address of Each IP in System

The base address of each IP in PD1 & PD2 are show as Table 1.

Table 1: Base address of each system IP

+-----------------+-------+--------------+
| Power Domain    | IP    | Base Address |
+=================+=======+==============+
| Power Domain 0\ | MISCL | 0x0400_0000  |
| (PD0)           |       |              |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | PADC  | 0x0400_0100  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | MUX   | 0x0400_0200  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | ANGC  | 0x0400_0300  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | CLK   | 0x0400_0400  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | PMU   | 0x0400_0500  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | RRAM  | 0x0400_0600  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | RTT   | 0x0400_0700  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | MISCH | 0x0400_1000  |
+-----------------+-------+--------------+
| Power Domain 1\ | MISCL | 0x0400_2000  |
| (PD1)           |       |              |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | PADC  | 0x0400_2100  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | GPIO  | 0x0400_2200  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | RNG   | 0x0400_2300  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | EFUC  | 0x0400_2400  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | I2C   | 0x0400_2500  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | RTT   | 0x0400_2600  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | WDT   | 0x0400_2700  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | MISCH | 0x0400_3000  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | ITC   | 0x0400_3100  |
|                 +-------+--------------+
|                 | UART  | 0x0400_3200  |
+-----------------+-------+--------------+

Register Spec

Configuration Register Type

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Attribute    Description
  ------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RO           Read-only register: Register bits are read-only and cannot be altered by software. Register bits may be initialized by hardware mechanisms such as pin strapping or serial EEPROM. IP Reset can't clear status of this type register.

  WO           Write-only register: Register bits are write-only.

  RW           Read-Write register: Register bits are read-write and may be either set or cleared by software to the desired state.

  RW1C         Read-only status, Write-1-to-clear status register: Register bits indicate status when read, a set bit indicating a status event may be cleared by writing a 1. Writing a 0 to RW1C bits has no effect.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

> \[4:0\]: SR_HWCFG

- This field is use to configure particular GPIO and JTAG ports

- SR_HWCFG\[0\] : disable JTAG function on JTAG ports

<!-- -->

- 0 : enable

- 1 : diable

<!-- -->

- SR_HWCFG\[1\] : disable UART function on GPIO\[1:0\]

<!-- -->

- 0 : enable

- 1 : diable

<!-- -->

- SR_HWCFG\[2\] : disable I2CS function on JTAG ports

<!-- -->

- 0 : enable

- 1 : diable

> \[31:18\]: Reserved
>
> \[17:16\]: CR_RRAM_RM

- Read-Write margin Input of RRAM

- This input is used for setting the Read-Write margin. It programs the sense amp differential setting. and allows the trade off between speed and robustness

- RM\[1:0\] = 2'b00 is the slowest possible mode of operation for the memory. This setting is require for VDDMIN operation

- RM\[1:0\] values control access time & cycle time of the memory. Refer to the timing table of each memory for more details

> \[15:12\]: Reserved
>
> \[11:8\]: SR_PD1_RAM_RM

- Read-Write margin Input of PD1 RAM (SATA)

- This input is used for setting the Read-Write margin. It programs the sense amp differential setting. and allows the trade off between speed and robustness

- RM\[1:0\] = 2'b00 is the slowest possible mode of operation for the memory. This setting is require for VDDMIN operation

- RM\[1:0\] values control access time & cycle time of the memory. Refer to the timing table of each memory for more details

> \[31\]: CR_TMS_S_CB

- Input setting of TMS

- Select Schmitt Trigger input / CMOS input

- Under VCC = 3.3V, CR_GPIO_GB_IO1 = 1

<!-- -->

- 0 : CMOS Trigger (Vih = Vil = 0.5 \* VCC)

- 1 : Schmitt Trigger (Vih = 0.65 \* VCC, Vil = 0.35 \* VCC)

<!-- -->

- Under VCC = 1.8V, CR_GPIO_GB_IO1 = 1

<!-- -->

- 0 : CMOS Trigger (Vih = Vil = 0.53 \* VCC)

- 1 : Schmitt Trigger (Vih = 0.69 \* VCC, Vil = 0.41 \* VCC)

> \[30\]: CR_TMS_SR

- Pre-driver slew rate control

<!-- -->

- 0 : Speed pre-driver buffer

- 1 : Slower pre-driver buffer

> \[29:28\]: CR_TMS_DV

- CR_TMS_DV \[0\]: Controlled 3mA driving current (High active)

>
> \[27:24\]: CR_VDT_TS_TEMP_SEL

<!-- -->

- 0000 \~ 1111 : -35 deg \~ 115 deg, 10 deg per step

> \[23:21\]: Reserved
>
> \[20:16\]: XVDT_TS_TCODE

- Temperature code to represent Temperature degree

<!-- -->

- 00000 : below -35 deg

- 00001 : -35 deg \~ -25 deg

- 00010 : -25 deg \~ -15 deg

- 00011 : -15 deg \~ -5 deg

- 00100 : -5 deg \~ 5 deg

- 00101 : 5 deg \~ -15 deg

- 00110 : 15 deg \~ 25 deg

- 00111 : 25 deg \~ 35 deg

- 01000 : 35 deg \~ 45 deg

- 01001 : 45 deg \~ 55 deg

- 01010 : 55 deg \~ 65 deg

- 01011 : 65 deg \~ 75 deg

- 01100 : 75 deg \~ 85 deg

- 01101 : 85 deg \~ 95 deg

- 01110 : 95 deg \~ 105 deg

- 01111 : 105 deg \~ 115 deg

- 10000 : beyond 115 deg

> \[21\]: CR_PLL_CHPMP_DIS\[0\]

- Disable charge pump of PLL0

- when reset PLL or open loop, need to set it to 1

<!-- -->

- 0 : normal

- 1 : disable charge pump

> \[20\]: CR_PLL_EN_VCMID\[0\]

- EN_VCMID of PLL0

- Force VCO to center of frequency. when reset PLL or open loop, need to set it to 1

<!-- -->

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

> \[19:16\]: Reserved
>
> \[15:0\]: CR_PLL_CFG\[79:64\]

- PLL1 configuration registers

> \[31\]: pre_sata_iso_en_wp

- Set this field to 1 means SATA controller will be power down

- H/W write 1 only

> \[30:8\]: Reserved
>
> \[7\]: cr_sata_gen_sel

- This field is used to select SATA speed control by GPIO or System

<!-- -->

- 0 : Control by gpio

- 1 : Control by system

> \[6\]: Reserved
>
> \[5:4\]: cr_sata_gen_f

- SATA link mode

<!-- -->

- 00 : OOB default on SATA Link Gen3

- 01 : OOB default on SATA Link Gen1

- 10 : OOB default on SATA Link Gen2

- 11 : OOB default off, FW enable OOB & SATA speed

> \[31:24\]: cr_fll_val

- The value apply to 1MHz generator counter (for FLL)

- User can set this field and let FLL clock approach to 1MHz

> \[23:16\]: sr_fll_val

- The value from 1MHz generator counter (for FLL)

- The value depends on the counter and its reference OSC clock

> \[15:8\]: Reserved
>
> \[7\]: phy_ref_cken_f

- Reference clock enable

<!-- -->

- 0 : the PD0 reference clock (ref. to XTAL (30MHz) or FLL clock (1MHz)) and all clock source of all clock generators in clock center will be gated

- 1 : the PD0 reference clock (ref. to XTAL (30MHz) or FLL clock (1MHz)) and all clock source of all clock generators in clock center are valid

> \[6\]: XPHY_REF_LOCK

- When SATA PHY OSC lock, this field will be set to 1

<!-- -->

- 0 : SATA PHY OSC unlock

- 1 : SATA PHY OSC lock

> \[5:2\]: Reserved
>
> \[1:0\]: SR_PLL_LOCK

- When PLL lock, this field will be set to 1

<!-- -->

- SR_PLL_LOCK\[0\] : PLL0 lock

- SR_PLL_LOCK\[1\] : PLL1 lock

> \[27:16\]: cr_wake_en

- Wake up enable source select

- Select wake up enable source when set the particular bits to 1

<!-- -->

- cr_wake_en \[0\] : wake up when DEVSLP = 0

- cr_wake_en \[1\] : wake up when DEVSLP = 1

- cr_wake_en \[2\] : wake up when falling edge of DEVSLP

- cr_wake_en \[3\] : wake up when rising edge of DEVSLP

- cr_wake_en \[4\] : wake up when GPIO = 0

- cr_wake_en \[5\] : wake up when GPIO = 1

- cr_wake_en \[6\] : wake up when falling edge of GPIO

- cr_wake_en \[7\] : wake up when rising edge of GPIO

- cr_wake_en \[8\] : wake up when RTT wake up enable

- cr_wake_en \[9\] : wake up when SATA wake up enable

- cr_wake_en \[10\] : wake up when ITC wake up enable

- cr_wake_en \[11\] :wake up when cr_pmu_wu_f be set to 1

> \[15:10\]: Reserved
>
> \[9\]: cr_gpio_det_en

- Detecting both rising and falling edge on GPIO

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

<!-- -->

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

- 01 : 64us

> \[31:2\]: Reserved
>
> \[1:0\]: CR_PD0_RAM_RM

- Read-Write margin Input of PD0 RAM (CPU resume DRAM)

- This input is used for setting the Read-Write margin. It programs the sense amp differential setting. and allows the trade off between speed and robustness

- RM\[1:0\] = 2'b00 is the slowest possible mode of operation for the memory. This setting is require for VDDMIN operation

- RM\[1:0\] values control access time & cycle time of the memory. Refer to the timing table of each memory for more details

>
> \[28:24\]: cr_vdt_det_en

- VDT edge detector enable

- Detect both rising edge and falling edge on signals below:

> cr_vdt_det_en\[0\]: XVDT_FIO_PG
>
> cr_vdt_det_en\[1\]: XVDT_IO0_PG
>
> cr_vdt_det_en\[2\]: XVDT_PD1_PG
>
> cr_vdt_det_en\[3\]: XVDT_PD2_PG
>
> cr_vdt_det_en\[4\]: XVDT_FLH_PG

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

> \[23:18\]: Reserved
>
> \[17:16\]: cr_ts_det_en

- Temperature sensor edge detector enable

- Detect both rising edge and falling edge on XVDT_TS_TEMP_HIGH and XVDT_TS_TCODE_DRY

> cr_ts_det_en\[0\]: XVDT_TS_TCODE_RDY
>
> cr_ts_det_en\[1\]: XVDT_TS_TEMP_HIGH

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

> \[15:11\]: Reserved
>
> \[10:8\]: cr_pll_lock_det_en

- PLL lock edge detector enable

- Detect both rising edge and falling edge on PLL lock

> cr_pll_lock_det_en\[0\]: SATA PHY PLL Lock
>
> cr_pll_lock_det_en\[1\]: PLL0 Lock
>
> cr_pll_lock_det_en\[2\]: PLL1 Lock

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

>

- 1 : enable

> \[7\]: GP1_DIR

<!-- -->

- 1: read data from I^2^C

- 0: write data to I^2^C

> \[6\]: GP1_A10_EN

<!-- -->

- 1: 10-bits address

- 0: 7-bits address

> \[5\]: PD1_CTRL

- This register indicates Power off 1 control and I^2^C will be triggered from the external signal.

<!-- -->

- 1: Enable power off 1 trigger

- 0: Disable power off 1 trigger

> \[4\]: GP1_BUF_SEL

- This register controls Group1 BUF select.

<!-- -->

- 1: Select BUF1

- 0: Select BUF0

> \[3\]: GP1_COMBI_MODE

- This register is set to enable Group1 combined mode.

<!-- -->

- 1: Combined mode

- 0: Normal mode.

<!-- -->

- Combined mode : s 🡪 Addr W 🡪 OP 🡪 rs 🡪 Addr W 🡪 Data 🡪 end

- Normal mode : s 🡪 Addr W 🡪 OP 🡪 Data 🡪 end

> NOTE: This bit is only for I^2^C write.
>
> \[2\]: GP1_HS_MODE

- This register is set to enable Group1 high speed mode.

<!-- -->

- 1: high speed mode

- 0: full speed mode

> \[1\]: GP1_DONE_INT_EN

- This register is set to enable Group1 I^2^C done interrupt. When group1 I^2^C finishes read/write and this bit is set to 1, HW will launch an interrupt (INT_REG\[0\] = 1), and then FW writes 0 into INT_REG\[0\] to clear interrupt.

<!-- -->

- 1: Enable done interrupt

- 0: Disable done interrupt

> \[0\]: GP1_I2C_START

- This register is set to start I^2^C and the data is auto cleared when I^2^C finishes.

- 00010 : reset SATA only when watch dog timeout

- 01000 : reset FLH, DBUF, AXI, SS, DMAC when watch dog timeout

- 10000 : reset DDR only when watch dog timeout

> \[31:0\]: CR_PD1_RAM_RM\[31:0\]

- Read-Write margin Input of PD1 RAM

- This input is used for setting the Read-Write margin. It programs the sense amp differential setting. and allows the trade off between speed and robustness

- This field indicates system interrupt events

- The value of each bit of this field will be valid when the particular interrupt enable in SYS_INT_ENx be set to 1

- The related interrupt events of each bit:

<!-- -->

- CPU_INT\[26\] : GPIO/VDT interrupt events (NMI) (see [SYS_INT_EN5](#SYS_INT_EN5))

- CPU_INT\[22\] : DDR ECC interrupt events (level3) (see [DDR_INT](#DDR_INT))

- CPU_INT\[21\] : PMU/PLL/GPIO/JTAG/TS/VDT interrupt events (level3) (see [SYS_INT_STS4](#SYS_INT_STS4))

- CPU_INT\[20\] : CPU/SATA/DMAC/RRAM/DBUF/DDR/Flash parity error

> interrupt events (level3) (see [SYS_INT_STS3](#SYS_INT_STS3))

- CPU_INT\[19\] : Stack monitoring interrupt events (see [cpu_intf](#cpu_intf))

- CPU_INT\[11\] : Flash message dispatch interrupt events (see [msg_int](#msg_int))

- CPU_INT\[9\] : RS interrupt events (level2) (see [RS_INT](#RS_INT))

- CPU_INT\[7\] : I2C interrupt events (level2) (see [i2cm_int](#i2cm_int))

- CPU_INT\[6\] : RTT0/RTT1/WDT interrupt events (level2) (see [SYS_INT_STS1](#SYS_INT_STS1))

- CPU_INT\[5\] : SATA interrupt events (level2) (see [SATA_INT](#SATA_INT))

- CPU_INT\[3\] : UART interrupt events (level2) (see [UART_INT](#UART_INT))

  1.  []{#_Toc410156364 .anchor}**UART (0x0400_3200 \~ 0x0400_32FF)**

      1.  []{#_Toc410156365 .anchor}**Functional Descriptions**

The UART controller is used to communicate with external devices. For PS3110, UART controller provides two modes to transmit and receive packet. One is normal mode in which UART controller will transmit and receive data as what user sets and what partner sends. The other one is OOB mode in which UART controller will transmit packet which data has been packed according to OOB packet format, and extract data from received OOB packet.

[Normal Mode TX:]{.underline}

There are two kind of operation methods for Normal mode of transmit:

1.  User should set up the entire data payload in dedicated register and then trigger UART controller to transmit packet.

2.  Figure 2 shows the firmware (FW) flow of transmitted packet through the first normal mode.

>
>
> Figure 2: Normal TX, Pre Set up Data

3.  Users can enter serial mode to write data into dedicated FIFO, and then UART controller will transmit data until FIFO is empty. Figure 3 shows the FW flow of transmitted packet through serial normal mode.

Figure 3: Normal TX, via Serial Data

[Normal Mode RX:]{.underline}

> While UART controller receives a normal packet from partner, the controller will record packet status in interrupt status register such as UR_RX_NOT_EMPTY_INT, and then trigger INT_N to notify FW that there is RX packet needs to be processed. Figure 4 shows the flow of receiving a normal packet.

Figure 4: Normal RX

[OOB Mode TX:]{.underline}

> Basically, transmitting OOB mode packet is the same as normal mode; the minor difference is that user needs to enable OOB_EN, and set up oob packet type respectively. Figure 5 shows the flow of transmitting an oob packet.

Figure 5: OOB TX

[OOB Mode RX:]{.underline}

Receiving OOB packet is terribly different from normal packet.

1.  There is a specific register to record packet status OOB rx.

2.  UART controller has dedicated 16 bytes space to save OOB packet; hence user could read data from register without checking FIFO status. 6 shows how to handle OOB RX packet.

Figure 6 OOB RX

> \[31\]: rx_reset

- This register is used to clear RX circuit when error happens, such as OOB Packet Framing Error. Users can set 1 to reset rx fifo, state machine and counter and then it will be auto-cleared by HW

> \[30:28\]: RX_LAT_POSI

- This register controls RX latch position and it is used to change UART RX latch data phase

> \[27\]: TX_BAUD_EN

- This register is set to enable/disable TX baud rate unit

<!-- -->

- 0 : disable TX baud rate generate Unit

- 1 : Enable TX baud rate generate Unit

> \[26\]: RX_BAUD_EN

- This register is set to enable/disable RX baud rate unit

<!-- -->

- 0 : Disable RX baud rate generate Unit

- 1 : Enable RX baud rate generate Unit

> \[25\]: INT_MASK_EN

- Enable interrupt mask to mask other interrupt source when data transfer

<!-- -->

- 0 : disable

- 1 : enable

> \[24\]: OOB_EN

- This register controls enabling/disabling OOB function. Before setting this bit, please ensure the trigger is off and all data have been sent

> \[23:0\]: BAUD_RATE

- This register controls the baud rate value. (3 bytes)

<!-- -->

- Ex: If REF_CLK=40Mhz and the desired value is (40e6/(115.2e3\*4))=0x56, the BAUD_RATE will be 0x56

  ------------ ---------- ------------------ ------------ ------------------- ---------------- --------------------- ----------------- -----------------
  Bit Symbol    Reserved   pkt_tx_cmplt_int   pkt_rx_int   pkt_start_err_int   pkt_to_err_int   pkt_framing_err_int   pkt_len_err_int   pkt_crc_err_int

  Default          0b             0b              0b              0b                 0b                 0b                  0b                0b

  Attribute        RO             RW              RW              RW                 RW                 RW                  RW                RW
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

> \[31:12\]: Reserved
>
> \[11\]: tx_cmplt_int

- Tx complete Interrupt. FW check this bit to make sure all TX bytes are sent to UART IF

> \[10\]: rx_not_empty_int

- This register indicates that RX data is in data fifo and RX_fifo is not empty

> \[9\]: rx_ovflw_int

- This register controls the overflow flag for receiving data

<!-- -->

- 1 : a character has been received during RX FULL

> \[8\]: rx_frame_err_int

- This register controls the received frame error

<!-- -->

- 1 : a stop bit was not detected in the end of frame

> \[7\]: Reserved
>
> \[6\]: pkt_tx_cmplt_int

- This register indicates OOB Packet Transmit has been completed and FW will check this bit to ensure all OOB Packets are sent to UART IF

> \[5\]: pkt_rx_int

- This register indicates that OOB packet has been received and the packet payload is in RX Payload register

> \[4\]: pkt_start_err_int

- This register indicates the OOB Packet Start Marker Error. Coming from interface idle, any non-ASCII value but 0xF1 is a packet start error

> \[3\]: pkt_to_err_int

- This register indicates the OOB Packet Timeout Error and End Packet Marker is received over Frame Timeout Period. (The default is 5ms)

> \[2\]: pkt_framing_err_int

- This register indicates the OOB Framing Error. The very next byte on the interface after Length bytes must be the end packet marker. (0xF7)

> \[1\]: pkt_len_err_int

- This register indicates the OOB Packet Length Error. If the received value of Length of Packet is less than 2 or more than 8, this bit will be asserted

> \[0\]: pkt_crc_err_int

- This register indicates the OOB Packet CRC check error and the CRC value is not correct. (CRC-8-CCITT)
